sdg.name: Life on Land
sdg.commitment: Take an active role in protecting and promoting sustainable use of terrestrial ecosystems, responsible land use, and biodiversity conservation.

indicators.title: Research on land ecosystems
indicators.question: Scholarly research on terrestrial ecosystems, forests, biodiversity, soils and land degradation.
indicators.note: THE takes the research metrics for SDG 15 from Scopus bibliometric data. Institutions do not upload documents for this metric, so the entries below are MMSU's research record on land ecosystems, kept for the team and for checking author affiliations. They are not submitted to THE.

metrics.heading: Supporting land ecosystems through education
metrics.group: PROJECTS AND ACTIVITIES: SUPPORTING LAND ECOSYSTEMS THROUGH EDUCATION

indicators.title: Events about sustainable use of land
indicators.question: Support or organise events aimed to promote conservation and sustainable utilisation of the land, including forests and wild land.

indicators.title: Sustainably farmed food on campus (policy)
indicators.question: Have a policy that food on campus is sustainably farmed.

indicators.title: Maintain and extend current ecosystems' biodiversity
indicators.question: Work directly to maintain and extend existing ecosystems and their biodiversity, of both plants and animals, especially ecosystems under threat.

indicators.title: Educational programmes on ecosystems
indicators.question: Offer educational programmes on ecosystems (looking at wild flora and fauna) for local or national communities.

indicators.title: Sustainable management of land for agriculture (educational outreach)
indicators.question: Offer educational programme/outreach for local or national communities on sustainable management of land for agriculture.

indicators.title: Sustainable management of land for tourism (educational outreach)
indicators.question: Offer educational programme/outreach for local or national communities on sustainable management of land for tourism.

indicators.title: Sustainable use, conservation and restoration of land (policy)
indicators.question: Have a policy to ensure the conservation, restoration and sustainable use of terrestrial ecosystems associated with the university, in particular forests, mountains and drylands.

indicators.title: Monitoring IUCN and other conservation species (policy)
indicators.question: Have a policy to ensure that IUCN Red List species and national conservation list species with habitats in areas affected by university operations are identified, monitored and protected.

indicators.title: Local biodiversity included in planning and development
indicators.question: Include local biodiversity into any planning and development process (e.g. construction of new buildings).

indicators.title: Alien species impact reduction (policy)
indicators.question: Have a policy to reduce the impact of alien species on campus.

indicators.title: Collaboration for shared land ecosystems
indicators.question: Collaborate with the local community to maintain shared land ecosystems.

indicators.title: Water discharge guidelines and standards
indicators.question: Have water quality standards and guidelines for water discharges (to uphold water quality in order to protect ecosystems, wildlife, and human health and welfare).

indicators.title: Policy on plastic waste reduction
indicators.question: Have a policy on reducing plastic waste on campus.

indicators.title: Policy on hazardous waste disposal
indicators.question: Have a policy, process or practice on waste disposal covering hazardous materials.

15.1.title: From wild foods to policy innovation: MMSU's indigenous food plants program as a model for sustainable and inclusive agriculture
15.1.people: Menisa A. Antonio, Ma. Concepcion Birginias, Josefa Pugat, Maingeline Vivit, Ruby Rose Tamayo
15.1.summary: Best Paper, sustainable and smart agri-aquaculture and climate resilience category, 2025 SUC-ACAP Biennial Conference and General Assembly (27 to 29 August 2025, Tagbilaran City, Bohol). The paper covers conservation of wild food plants through in situ, ex situ and circa situ approaches and the adoption of the program by the Regional Development Council of Region 1.
15.1.note: Conference paper; Scopus indexing not checked.

15.1.title: Nature-based Solutions (NbS) for Sustainable Mangrove Management and Resilient Coastal Communities Through Innovative Green Engineering Approach
15.1.people: Dr. Arlene L. Gonzales (Project Leader), with DENR-PENRO Ilocos Norte, the Provincial Government and the LGUs of Badoc and Currimao
15.1.summary: DOST-PCAARRD-funded project (1 May 2024 to 30 April 2026) in Badoc and Currimao, Ilocos Norte. It addresses the poor hydrological conditions that keep young mangrove propagules from surviving, using technology-assisted plantations and bamboo-engineered structures.
15.1.note: Coastal ecosystem; the team may weigh it under SDG 14 as well.

15.1.title: Enhancing the productivity of rice-based cropping systems through soil health management (Project SLaM 2023/146)
15.1.people: Dr. Janet Villamor (MMSU project lead), with Griffith University, ACIAR and DOST-PCAARRD
15.1.summary: MMSU joined a five-year program to develop soil knowledge and capacity for more productive and sustainable cropping systems. It evaluates nutrient management and develops yield-calibrated soil health indices for rice-garlic, rice-rice and rice-onion systems in Ilocos Norte, Tarlac and Bataan.
15.1.note: Agricultural soil research; confirm it falls under THE's land-ecosystems keywords.

15.1.title: Characterization and Evaluation of Indigenous Food Plant Species
15.1.people: Menisa A. Antonio, Bjorn S. Santos, Maria Concepcion Birginias, Jomel Agreda, Bella Gervacio
15.1.summary: Study under the parent project "Strengthening the Resilience of Iloco Crop Diversity Through Complementary Conservation Approach", with related studies on ex situ conservation facilities and community foodscapes and seedbanks. Status: extended.

15.1.title: Documentation of Dipterocarp Species in Second Growth Forest of Ilocos Norte
15.1.summary: Expected outputs: a handbook of dipterocarp species in Ilocos Norte and a map of dipterocarp forest. Status: extended.

15.1.title: Assessment and selection of suitable indigenous timber species under denuded hilly areas in Ilocos Norte
15.1.people: Charito Samsam, Sergia Garma, Joselito Rosario, Roseller Ayson
15.1.summary: Completed study under the parent project on species-site suitability of indigenous timber species in denuded areas, with a related performance evaluation of promising species under different management strategies on hilly denuded land.

15.1.title: Phenology of Broussonetia luzonica (Blanco) Bur.: A Promising Indigenous Vegetable
15.1.people: Menisa A. Antonio, Evangeline S. Galacgac, Rodel T. Utrera
15.1.summary: Best Poster, 2019 Plant Biology Forum, University of the Philippines Los Baños (29 to 30 April 2019). The study characterised alukon (himbabao) trees in four ecological zones of Ilocos Norte: morphology, reproductive characters, growth stages and flowering habit.

15.1.title: Resource Assessment and Evaluation of Dipterocarps and Premium Indigenous Timber Species in Ilocos Norte
15.1.summary: Completed project that located and documented superior mother trees of dipterocarps and other indigenous timber species in Ilocos Norte and evaluated their phenotypic qualities and phenology.

15.1.title: Documentation of Dipterocarp Species in Second Growth Forest in Selected Municipalities of Ilocos Norte
15.1.people: Charlie Batin, Roseller Ayson, Dionisio Jamias, Erle Stanley Damaso, Mary Ann Gorospe
15.1.summary: Documentation of dipterocarp trees dominating second-growth forests in Nueva Era, Pasuquin, Vintar, Adams and Pagudpud, with diameter, species and stocking data. Status: deferred.

15.1.title: Resource Assessment of Existing Potential Biofuel-Source Species in Ilocos Norte
15.1.people: Joselito Rosario, Charito Samsam, Dionisio Jamias, Sergia Garma
15.1.summary: Completed project that built a database of energy-producing tree species in Region I through exploration, identification, abundance and phenology studies, with DENR, DA and local governments.
15.1.note: Related; energy-tree species rather than conservation.

15.1.title: Survey and Characterization of Indigenous Food Plants in Ilocos Norte, Philippines
15.1.people: Menisa A. Antonio, Rodel T. Utrera, Epifania O. Agustin, Dionisio L. Jamias, Araceli J. Badar, Miriam E. Pascua
15.1.summary: SEARCA Agriculture and Development Discussion Paper No. 2011-2 (61 pages). Documented 46 indigenous food plants from 27 families in seven upland and remote municipalities, most of them wild species, and reported that MMSU maintains their germplasm as living plants and seeds.
15.1.note: Discussion paper; Scopus indexing not checked.

15.1.title: Survey and characterization of indigenous food plants in Ilocos Norte, Philippines
15.1.people: Menisa Antonio, Rodel T. Utrera, Epifania O. Agustin
15.1.summary: Completed program (1 November 2008 to 20 June 2010) that produced the 2011 SEARCA discussion paper.

15.1.title: MMSU researchers identify vanishing plant species
15.1.people: Dr. Miriam Pascua, Menisa Antonio, Dionisio Bucao and colleagues
15.1.summary: Survey of Laoag City, Batac, Pasuquin, San Nicolas and Dingras: of 124 plants that elders perceived to be vanishing, 77 were validated as such using IUCN criteria, 45 classified as endangered and 32 as vulnerable.
15.1.note: The classification applied IUCN criteria locally; it is not the IUCN Red List.

15.1.title: Natural Resources Conservation and Management Center (NRCMC)
15.1.people: Center Chief: Mae Ann R. Batuyong
15.1.summary: MMSU's research hub for the conservation of flora and fauna in the Ilocos Region. It leads R&D on plant genetic resources characterization, conservation of plants, animals and water resources, forest resource conservation and fishery resource management.
